title: Mansa Musa — the pilgrimage that broke a currency
style: documentary photograph, 14th century West Africa and Egypt, warm desert light, muted earth and gold, fine grain, period-accurate, no text, no watermark, no modern objects
$note: Written by hand: the voiceover, and one phrase per line saying what we are looking at. The planner derives everything else — shot type, length, look, cuts.

lines.vo: In thirteen twenty-four the ruler of Mali left home for Mecca, and took his treasury with him.
lines.image: a vast empty Sahara dune field at dawn, long shadows, nobody present
lines.title: HE TOOK IT ALL

lines.vo: Accounts describe tens of thousands of people on the road, and camels carrying gold by the hundredweight.
lines.image: a wide desert horizon at midday, heat haze over flat sand, empty
pieces: traveller in a long desert robe
caption: Tens of thousands
on the road.

lines.vo: In Cairo he did not trade the gold. He gave it away, to officials, to merchants, to the poor.
lines.image: an empty medieval Cairo market street of pale stone at noon, deep shadow under arches
items: card|TO THE COURT|robes and gifts to the sultan's officials
card|TO THE MARKET|paid above price, and kept paying
card|TO THE POOR|handed out in the street, every district
caption: He did not
trade it.

lines.vo: He spent so freely that the price of gold in Cairo fell, and one contemporary writer found it still had not recovered twelve years later.
lines.image: a dim stone counting room with scales and scattered coins, one shaft of daylight
lines.title: TWELVE YEARS
lines.footer: and by one account it had still not recovered

lines.vo: On the road home he brought back an architect, and Timbuktu got a mosque of mud brick and timber.
lines.image: a tall mud-brick mosque wall with projecting wooden beams, hard desert sun
lines.artefact: a close view of a mud-brick wall studded with protruding palm timbers, warm raking light

lines.vo: Fifty years later a mapmaker in Europe drew him on a chart, seated, holding a nugget of gold.
lines.image: an old vellum chart on a wooden table, dividers and an inkpot beside it
lines.artefact: a detail of a medieval illuminated map on vellum, gold leaf and faded ink, cracked surface
caption: Drawn by
someone who
never met him.

lines.vo: He is often called the richest man who ever lived. Nobody can actually measure that.
lines.image: an empty desert night under heavy stars, cold blue sand
caption: Often called
the richest
who ever lived.

lines.vo: What can be measured is the damage. One pilgrimage, and a city's currency took a decade to come back.
lines.image: a single set of footprints crossing an empty dune, wind erasing them
lines.title: ONE PILGRIMAGE
